\begin{theorem}\label{thm:rectangle}
Let $E$ be an ellipse with center $O$, semiaxes $a>b>0$, and either
focus $F$. Let $R$ be any rectangle whose four sides are supporting
tangents of $E$. The antipedal of $R$ with respect to $F$ is a finite
strictly convex quadrilateral, and its centroids are
\[
       C_0=O,\qquad C_2=O+\frac{F-O}{3}.
\]
In particular, both points are independent of the rectangle's
orientation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}\label{cor:source}
Let $P$ range over a primitive four-periodic billiard family inside
a fixed ellipse, with a strictly nested confocal elliptic caustic.
Let $P'$ be the outer polygon formed by consecutive boundary-tangent
intersections. For either focus $F$, the vertex and signed-area
centroids of the antipedal of $P'$ are $O$ and $O+(F-O)/3$.
\end{corollary}
